about: The science bench: hard maths and physics questions, asked in English (the Turkish originals are kept as separate tables at the end of the list). University maths & physics: 50 problems (25 maths, 25 physics) from university textbooks and exams, every given number changed and the answer recomputed by code, five options of which four are typical mistakes. High-school maths: 32 questions from the first stage of a 2026 national high-school maths olympiad, with its official answer key; public since May 2026, so a model trained on later data may have seen them. Broken questions: the 50 university problems mixed with 42 copies in which one given number was changed so that none of the five options is right (checked by code), with a sixth option F 'the question is flawed'; right means F on a broken copy and the right option on an intact one. Exact answers: the same 50 university problems with no options; the model writes the number, right when within 0.1% of the code's value; a reply that is not a number counts wrong. Latency and cost: on our GPU, median seconds per problem with the requests in flight shown, and GPU time from start to last answer × $2.49 per GPU-hour per 1,000 problems; subscription routes, the tokens they reported at the maker's API list price, nothing billed. Decision and small models were asked one question per request; the subscription models (Claude, GPT, Gemini, MAI) 16 per request through their own tools, marked batched where it matters. The English text was translated from the Turkish originals by Gemini 4 Neon and checked again by GPT-6.2 Astra, every number compared by code. The questions are not published; right or wrong per problem for every run is in https://zekiworks.github.io/analysis/science/answers.json, for paired tests. A reply without a readable letter counts wrong.
